bib.title: On the Reliability Limits of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Planning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "On the Reliability Limits of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Planning", Ruicheng Ao, Siyang Gao, David Simchi-Levi (MIT, CityU HK). arXiv:2603.26993v1 [cs.MA], 27 Mar 2026 (dated 31 Mar 2026). It calls itself a "technical note". It is a preprint with no venue.

COVERAGE: All 59,330 chars were read, covering the main text, the proofs of Lemmas 1-5, Prop 6 and Thms 7-10, the experiment tables and Appendix A. I skimmed the references for origins. The extraction was clean, apart from the figure axes and the Table 2 layout.

CLAIMS (ranked)

- **Delegation ceiling (Prop 6).** For any finite DAG of agents, with exogenous signals E_exo=(B, Z_V) and ancillary randomness ξ independent of Y given E_exo, E[ℓ(A,Y)] ≥ V(E_exo;ℓ) for every bounded loss. So the network is dominated by a centralized Bayes decision maker who sees the same exogenous signals.
  - number: none (theorem)
  - setup: acyclic graph, standard Borel spaces, bounded ℓ, ξ ⊥ Y | E_exo. No new exogenous signal enters. The message rules and node rules are arbitrary.
  - quote: "Then for every bounded loss ℓ, E[ℓ(A, Y)] ≥ V(E_exo; ℓ). Equivalently, the delegated network is decision-theoretically dominated by a centralized Bayes decision maker observing the same exogenous signals E_exo."
  - where: p.9, Prop 6.
  - The proof says A is "a randomized garbling of E". Lemma 2 is the data-processing step: if M is generated from H by a kernel that is conditionally independent of Y given H, then V(M;ℓ) ≥ V(H;ℓ) (p.7). Lemma 4(a) restates it in Blackwell form (p.8).

- **Common-evidence reduction (Thm 7).** When no node has a private signal (Z_v=∅, E_exo=B), a multi-agent DAG is equivalent to a stochastic encoder Q(m|B). Under the communication budget C(G)=log|M_G|, inf over G of E[ℓ(A_G,Y)] = inf over finite-M encoders with log|M|≤C of V(M;ℓ).
  - number: none
  - setup: the budget is the cardinality of the terminal state that the output stage sees, not the transcript length.
  - quote: "a multi-agent directed acyclic graph is decision-theoretically equivalent to the finite experiment Q(m|B) that it induces on the shared signal."
  - where: p.10-11.
  - Remark 2: a structured interface that Blackwell-dominates free text weakly dominates it. "The relevant design object is not the role label but the experiment induced by the communication interface."
  - Remark 1: the problem is Bayesian persuasion, rational inattention or an information bottleneck. It is specific to common evidence. With genuinely private signals it becomes a team decision problem, where Witsenhausen (1968) shows the reduction fails.

- **Communication loss equals posterior distortion (Thm 8).** For a proper scoring rule s, V(M;s) − V(H;s) = E[D_s(π_H, π_M)] ≥ 0. This holds when M=μ(H,ζ) with ζ ⊥ Y | H and Y finite.
  - Under log loss the gap is I(Y;H|M) = E[KL(π_H‖π_M)]. Under the Brier score it is E‖π_H − π_M‖²₂.
  - On a serial chain Y→M0→…→ML under log loss, the loss is additive: Σ I(Y;M_{ℓ−1}|M_ℓ).
  - If s is strictly proper, the gap is zero iff π_H=π_M almost surely.
  - quote: "the cost of communication is exactly the amount by which communication distorts the posterior used for the final decision."
  - where: p.12-14.
  - Remark 4: transcript length, number of roles and number of rounds are the wrong proxies. "a longer multi-stage system need not be worse if the extra stage preserves the posterior."

- **Test for whether a stage adds information (Cor 9).** Adding a verifier signal W gives V((M,W);ℓ) ≤ V(M;ℓ). The inequality is strict for some bounded loss iff (M,W) is not Blackwell-dominated by M, meaning W is not redundant given M.
  - quote: "self-critique that only re-reads M cannot move the Bayes envelope, but executable tests or external validators can."
  - where: p.14-15.

- **Selective review (Thm 10).** The optimal value is E[min{R_a(H), R_h(H)}]. Escalate when the automated posterior risk exceeds the review loss.
  - Remark 5: do not trigger review by stage count, by disagreement alone, or by blanket rules.
  - where: p.15-16.

- **Evaluation warning (Remark 3).** Architecture comparisons that change tools, retrieval or workspace size at the same time cannot separate an architecture effect from an information change. Compare under matched exogenous signals and matched terminal state capacity.
  - where: p.11.

- **Empirical: relay without new signal collapses accuracy.**
  - number: gpt-4.1-mini goes from 90.7% (A') to 41.2% (2-agent), 43.5% (3-agent) and 22.5% (5-agent). o4-mini goes from 89.9% to 37.0% at 3 agents.
  - setup: 200 four-way MMLU questions, balanced across categories. 30 runs per question for A, B, C, D and S, and 10 runs for B2, B5, Bpost and Dsame. Downstream relay stages never see the original question. Prose relay. N is 1,993-6,000 runs, with CI half-widths of .007-.027.
  - quote: "Ongpt-4.1-mini, accuracy falls from90.7%in(A)to41.2%in(B 2),43.5%in(B), and22.5%in(B 5). Ono4-mini, the analogous drop from(A)to(B)is from 89.9%to37.0%."
  - where: p.17, Table 2.
  - The 5-agent result is "numerically below the 25% chance level".

- **Empirical: structured interface preserves information.**
  - number: 75.2% for a 3-stage posterior-vector relay against 58.1% for a 3-stage prose relay. Degradation is about 2.8 vs 8.5 points per stage.
  - setup: 50 MMLU questions, n=750 per condition, gpt-4.1-mini.
  - quote: "At three stages,(Bpost)reaches75.2%accuracy compared with58.1%for(B)."
  - where: p.18-19, Fig 3.

- **Empirical: redundant tools do not help, non-redundant ones do.**
  - number: MMLU single agent + Wikipedia 87.2%. Wikipedia + Semantic Scholar specialists 89.8%. Two Wikipedia specialists 89.8%. Synthetic KB without the tool 24.3%, with the tool 82.7%.
  - setup: gpt-4.1-mini. The synthetic task has 200 fictional entities unknown to the model, so the tool is required.
  - quote: "tool access raises accuracy from24.3%to82.7%."
  - where: p.17-19, Table 2 and Fig 4.

- **Empirical: distortion correlates with accuracy loss.**
  - number: per-question correlation between KL(π_A‖π_B) and accuracy drop is r=0.72 for the 3-agent relay and r=0.44 for the 5-agent relay.
  - setup: gpt-4.1-mini only, because o4-mini exposes no logprobs. Posteriors are token logprobs from an "If you had to answer now" probe.
  - quote: "The correlation isr=0.72for condition(B)andr=0.44for condition(B 5)."
  - where: p.18.

LIMITS
- **Theory scope.** The results hold for the common-evidence regime, or when no new exogenous signal arrives. The authors concede that with private signals "the reduction no longer applies".
- **Model level.** The model works at the level of information structure, not token generation. It says nothing about compute. It does not cover reasoning models that spend more inference compute on the same evidence, or test-time scaling, which the intro notes can help. Prop 6 does not rule out gains from parallel samples or aggregation. If a node's randomness is independent of Y given E_exo, a randomized garbling cannot beat Bayes either.
- **Experiments.** They use MMLU, which the authors admit "is not a planning benchmark". Only two OpenAI models were tested, and the Wikipedia tool was largely redundant on MMLU. The relay deliberately hides the original question, so the collapse measures a worst-case bottleneck, not typical multi-agent designs. The posteriors are proxies, and the authors say "the plot should be interpreted qualitatively". No multi-agent condition shows a gain over the single agent.
- **Internal inconsistencies, flagged here.**
  - The 58.1% for 3-stage prose (50-question subset, Fig 3) conflicts with 43.5% in Table 2 (full set).
  - Fig 4 labels MMLU as 82.4 and 87, while the text gives a 90.7 baseline and "+3.8pts".
  - Table 2 lists A' at .907 and A (o4-mini) at .899.
  - Check these before quoting any single figure.
- **Dated.** The paper is a v1 preprint from March 2026. The related empirical papers it cites are Kim 2025, Xu 2026 and Wan 2025, and it does not engage the later literature.

BUILDS ON
- Team decision theory: Radner 1962 (Ann. Math. Stat.), Marschak & Radner 1972 (Economic Theory of Teams), Ho & Chu 1972 (IEEE TAC).
- Blackwell comparison of experiments: Blackwell 1953, Torgersen 1991.
- Proper scoring rules: Gneiting & Raftery 2007 (JASA).
- Reject-option classification: Chow 1970, El-Yaniv & Wiener 2010.
- Bayesian persuasion: Kamenica & Gentzkow 2011.
- Rational inattention: Sims 2003.
- Information bottleneck: Tishby et al. 2000.
- Witsenhausen 1968.
- Measurable selection: Bertsekas & Shreve 1978.
- LLM context: Cemri et al. 2025 (arXiv 2503.13657, MAS failures), Xia et al. 2024 (Agentless), Kim et al. 2025 (arXiv 2512.08296), Wan et al. 2025 (ICML, multi-agent debate), Wynn et al. 2025, Xu et al. 2026 (arXiv 2601.12307, single-agent baseline), Huang et al. 2024 (ICLR, self-correction without external feedback).

CODE: none. The prompt templates are in Appendix A.2, Boxes 1-5, p.24-26. Box 3 is the posterior-vector relay: "Output ONLY four numbers separated by spaces, your probability estimates for choices A, B, C, and D respectively. The four numbers must sum to 1.0."

FIGURES
- Candidate: Figure 1, p.18, "Accuracy versus relay length on MMLU (200 questions). A single agent achieves ∼90% on both models. Each additional communication stage degrades accuracy. At five agents, performance falls below the 25% chance baseline." It shows the cost of stages that add no signal at a glance.
- Alternatives: Fig 3 (p.19, prose relay vs posterior relay) and Fig 4 (p.20, redundant vs non-redundant tool).

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions were found in the PDF. Equations and figure axes are garbled in the extraction, so the formulas above were read from the extracted text. The figures were not rendered. The numeric inconsistencies are listed under LIMITS. The first extraction was saved at /tmp/ao_part2.txt for chars 30000 onward.
